verdict.justification: Both deliverables correctly resolve the workspace governance conflict by applying the approved USD 5,000 budget threshold from `operations/record-r2.txt` instead of the unapproved USD 50,000 proposal. However, Deliverable A is significantly more thorough, polished, and usable across all three files. In the SOP, Deliverable A follows the exact section order requested in the Working Session Summary (including a clear 10-step numbered procedure in Section 6 separate from the approval logic in Section 7) and includes a comprehensive reconciliation table in Section 10 with assigned owners. In the Change Request Form, Deliverable A provides a superior layout with explicit trigger screening checkboxes (`Section C – Change Screening`), a structured table for version-controlled attachments (`Section E – Attachments`), and separate approval tables for formal (`F1. Formal pathway`) vs. fast-track (`F2. Fast-track pathway`) routes. In contrast, Deliverable B's form has minor formatting/concatenation flaws (e.g., `☐ Yes  ☐ NoDetail`, `1.2.3.` for attachments) and combines both approval pathways into a single table. Finally, Deliverable A's Excel tracker is better structured as a controlled document template with header metadata and clearly labeled supporting columns (`Review Pathway` and `Signed Form Archive Reference`).
